sections: The visual grammar to carry forward

rules.lesson: Establish the premise, cut to a physically different camera position, then finish tighter. A crop or digital zoom is not a new angle.
rules.adaptation: Use three distinct front-facing or three-quarter camera positions, keeping the chest readable.

rules.lesson: Bind character identity, garment construction and props to distinct reference roles. Keep identity and world consistent.
rules.adaptation: Character and environment are locked. Only the selected upper-body garment is a brand variable.

rules.lesson: Build toward a tighter character-focused punchline and stop after it.
rules.adaptation: End on one short category-neutral line. Add brand URL in postproduction without a new spoken read.

rules.lesson: A recurring game-world character and one comic observation can lead naturally into a worn apparel product.
rules.adaptation: Use original lines and an original recurring character. Avoid named creator slogans, performance promises and product-specific speech.

rules.lesson: Specific game/social rituals and a simple visible action carry recognition. Keep product actions physically simple.
rules.adaptation: Turn a quick errand, default-skin joke or wardrobe menu into an original short setup and payoff.

rules.lesson: A specific observation, one escalation and one payoff work inside a consistent original world. Keep the first shot legible and hand actions simple.
rules.adaptation: Compose a stable front-facing apparel scene with three real camera angles. Keep the garment readable and bind the same product across shots.
